Dtide chatter:

In anticipation of Caraboo next monday, this week is Caro ring as expected.
Notably, both W4 and W5 boss has the burn gimmick, which are unique to these two awakener boss atm, perhaps caraboo is able to counter this somehow?

Overall difficulty imo is W4 = W5 > W3 > W2 > W1,  but W5 will be a lot easier if you have a built Glotan.

------------------------------

Wave 1: “Schizophrenic”, relic：Rhind Papyrus
W1 boss is the schizophrenic patient from Clem’s chapter,，he only has 1 health bar , but its a big one, sitting at a massive value at 2002K hp, though his is pretty easy and is fairly abusable.

His rotation goes something like this:

Please refer to the attached image on "Schizophrenic” for moveset

Exploration Note:

You need to go through at least 2 battle before you can face the boss

The path through the portal will lead you to a shop, while the back track path will lead to a healing tile, but also an extra fight

Battle Note:

Mr Schizo is fairly simple: he has a pseudo berserk passive and loses str when he gets hit.

On 15 accumulated card use in a single turn, his intention will be switched to “Trauma Blow”, a big single hit that applies 1 turn of Trauma to you.

Trauma: when you play a strike, shuffle a wound to the top of your drawpile

Whenever Mr Schizo gets hit, he loses 37 temp str

Which means if your playing a comp that does a lot of multihit (like Aequor tentacle comps), you can quite reliably lower his damage to an acceptable number

Interestingly, on turn 4 Mr schizo will give himself old ember, which means he will take more damage each turn from that point onward.

Potential strategy against this guy:
Xu:  Mr Schizo is a humanoid enemy, which means Xu’s % max health damage from removing stacks is twice as effective. With caro ring, Xu can apply these stacks fairly fast too, so you could just cheese the boss with Xu’s max health damage if you bring enough stall + multihit. Similarly, Gdoll’s max health damage is nice to have too. Bring Xu’s Posse for more passive stacks
Replay(Aequor Xu): ff641579-b4f7-3421-a6eb-e17599f0c22f#E#a
Replay(non-OE Gdoll Xu): db9332c9-4691-35a8-b4a1-ba84141c7997#E#a

Multihit comp: Boss loses temp str whenever he takes a hit, which means, the best defence is literally the best offense. There are a few ways you can do this, meta wise, the easiest pick is mouchette, but apart from that, it is also possible to clear with something like discard aurita or invested sorel pickman/tawil hamel. Though, do take note of his single big hit intention, that one just dont bother about lowering str,  you gotta live through it with DR.
Replay(Mouchette) : 9ed8f30c-199e-3caf-9871-55e49327a680#E#a
Replay(Aurita Discard): 7b1b444a-22e7-39a7-8769-7db2399bcd1f#E#a

Glotan: Mr Schizo hits really hard pass turn 4,  making him quite a good Glotan exalt target, though you probably would want to pack some DR so you could live till your big exalt turn.
Replay:  6e6c3ef3-415d-3108-9d23-66833d103374#E#a

Wave 2: Guard of Iensmo , relic：Safe Passage
W2 is the summoner Seafarer from chapter 6，an aequor enemy that is luckily not a tentacle enemy. She has a single hp bar,  with 1433K Hp.

Moveset:
Please refer to the attached image “Guard of Iensmo" for moveset.

Exploration Notes

The exploration this wave is a straight forward no-skipping pain train, you gotta fight all the mob fights except one optional fight right before the boss, luckily, they are not too difficult

Elite this wave is Host, he has a massive HP pool, but gains sacrifice stack whenever he takes damage, you can do a big burst early and wait for him to kill himself with sacrifice.

Boss Note:

This boss is a summoner, her main gimmick is that, Upon taking some amount of accumulated damage, she summons a mob in front of her, and this can happen multiple times. But she is limited to having at most 4 summons at the same time.

The summons have roughly 40K hp, they don't do a lot of damage, but will shuffle a bunch of random cards into your hand, which can be annoying, but the cards they give are mostly harmless.

It should be noted that “Child of Wafer” specifically will give you a stack of vulnerable on death, so be careful on your timing of when to kill it.

Boss has a ton of multihit attacks, and gains madness as the battle progresses, making counter a viable strategy.

Potential Strategy:

Counter: pretty much all of the boss’s attacks are multihits that are prone to str down, you can take advantage of this by playing a counter centric team against it. Pickman Caecus is especially effective into this boss, as pickman can steal strength from the mobs too. Wanda stall also works.
Replay(Pickman caecus): c113eb15-3f65-3439-a8ab-363feb6683e1#E#a
Replay(Wanda stall) : 6630fde7-93c3-3112-b26c-b5bc4e635714#E#a

Doresain : Doresain usually can perform decently in caro ring week, and the good news is, as a mob sweeper, he can be played into this wave pretty well. But this does require you to time your play order so that doresain gets the last hits on the summons
Replay(OE, no pickman): 4663e13b-879a-33f8-a1f1-edf88f08b28b#E#a
Replay(E2 with pickman): f258d3e5-c1d8-3812-9a65-4ccd788f5818#E#a

Castor Pollux: Classic W2 scaling comp, you don't really need OE on anyone, pollux does enough damage to beat down the boss even at E3, but you should at least have him leveled, since stats is his best form of scaling.
Replay:4eddc312-0e73-39b4-b423-7515281a9f7a#E#a

Wave 3:Clem, relic: Injector
W3 is Clem , an awakener boss with really annoying gimmick and damage to match. Unlike most other awakeners, she only has a single hp bar at 933K HP.

Moveset:
Please refer to the image “Hypnotic Shaggai” for moveset.

Exploration note:

W3 is direct to boss stage, theres no exploration

Battle note:

Clem has 2 very powerful passives, first being she hard limits your hand size to 8, even if you bring handsize wheels, and stops end of turn discard. 

Clem second passive is that, she takes 75% less damage on her own turn, this includes bleed poison counter and sacrifice, which is why i don't recommend Gmurphy lemurian or counter into this wave.

Poison is fine thou, since you have alot of poison trigger on your own turns.

On the first turn, clem does a big single hit nuke, and gain another passive that inflict dissolute paint to 2 of your random cards on turn start. Cards inflicted will have randomised cost (from -2 cost to +2 cost) and card text is obscured. having some form of cost reduction/card glowing gimmick (like Vortice reload and Xu's resonance) will help with navigating your hand

And now, the 4th gimmick of the fight, clem has 2 attacks that can be alternated by using an awakener's rouse.

The first one is a single big hit that gives clem 1 frenzy and the second one is a multihit that gives clem permanent str.

The idea is that, you need to use rouse on the right turn to alternate between Clem's intention and balance her ramp up between str and frenzy. But even then, she scales extremely fast.

On turn 6, clem will have a healing intent that applies weak and vulnerable to you, heal her for 10% missing hp, but also remove half of her frenzy and str she scaled up.

Of course, Clem herself can sort of counter herself, because her 2 cost is able to temporarily remove frenzy, making boss clem's damage that much more manageable.

Potential Strategy:

Mouchette: The fight with clem gets more annoying as fight goes on, since more and more of your card will have obscured card text, so finishing it fast is the best strategy, and mouchette is just the right woman for the job. You can have lv1 units with no wheels and just borrow a whale mouchette to solo carry on this wave.
Replay(standard mouchette clear): 0b138c2c-7d62-3e89-b87e-b304d747e08e#E#a

Replay(Whale borrow with lv1 units): 4b0f0fec-c727-3cdf-96cd-37e0e0da9be2#E#a

Gdoll Xu: Classic poison works great here, despite Str down is only half as effective on clem, its still a great way of lowering her damage,  plus you usually want to rouse 3 or more unit in poison comp anyway, so you could use that to your advantage to manipulate Clem’s intention. And of course, Caro xu is pretty op.

Replay: f0d9bdc4-c1ad-3db0-ad67-24f7d97a8217#E#a

Wave 4: Kath relic：Brotch
W4 is the awakener boss Kath, she's one of the only two enemies that has the burn mechanic. she has 2 health bars, with phase 1 having 739K hp and 1479K hp Phase 2. 

Moveset :
Please refer to the attached image “The living Flame**” for moveset**

Exploration note:

Wave 4 is an elite only wave, the two elites you encounter before the boss are “The Missing one” and “The Final Mire”

The Missing one, aka telephone mob is especially annoying due to his Perma weakness + fragile application and shield gain on non-command card play. This includes rouse, insight etc. The upside is that he has a lot of down time between attacks, which you can use to your advantage for scaling or setup

Final Mire similar to the telephone mob before him, also has weakness + Fragile application, but it  only last one turn, thou he is also more aggressive compared to telephone mob,  having an Atk -> Debuff -> Atk -> Defbuff rotation.

Battle note:

With all things considered, Kath is a pretty difficult boss. Not only does she have a big burst on hyperflare,  she also has a bunch of chip damage from her burn cards，and vulnerable application, making it almost impossible to avoid damage.

Her main gimmick revolves around the burn status, and her whole kit works around this.

Burn: when a card is burning, you will take damage when you play it, but if you don't play it, it will be exhausted at the end of turn.

Which means, you will need to tank the damage and play your burn cards to prevent them from exhausting.

Fortunately, Kath will lose str whenever you play a burn card, and the str down is more than the damage you receives from burn card, meaning you will always take lesser damage overall by playing the burn card.

For each burn card you played, kath will gain 1 stack of combust, and when she gets 10 stacks, her intention switches to the high burst “Hyperflare”

Note that, when she's on “Hyperflare”, str down and str gain are both double as effective, which means she will still be losing damage overall when you play a burn card.

On phase change, Kath will discard all your cards in hand, be ready for it

Normally, I would recommend Kath into Kath, to make use of the burn removal talent, but in this wave, it's really difficult for kath to survive the first two elites unscathed , so you might be better off playing something else.

Potential strategy:

Whale Gmurphy: Kath hits really hard, and gets more annoying in phase 2 due to her burn application，so skipping phase 2 with a whale Gmurphy becomes quite a decent strategy. Since this is one of the hardest wave this tide, its justifiable to use a borrow. but if you are willing to do some reseting for relic and what not, there is also this fairly low investment E3 Gmurphy clear i found, very impressive

Replay(whale borrow): 7077e143-975a-3559-b35c-f8b8f011a02b#E#a
Replay(e3): 7077e143-975a-3559-b35c-f8b8f011a02b#E#a

Ghelot: Ghelot works pretty well into this wave, countering the phone mob elite’s shielding and synergising pretty well with the relic, she also has in-built healing to deal with the burning damage. And If your flail is burning, might as well play it, you will likely heal more health than you lose .
Replay：d32af845-6b09-3d05-9cdf-7141d8a0586f#E#a

Honorable mention——All standard/welfare units clear: A clear with Gramona, Ogier, Doll and Nautila, even if rather high investment, but still very impressive.
Replay: 92f841e9-5986-3df9-a977-a49c0040c9a4#E#a

Wave 5: Liz：Vision Corrector
W5 is Liz, the only other enemy with a burn gimmick. As an awakener boss, she also has 2 phases, with 1121K hp in phase 1 and 1681K in phase 2.  A formidable foe, that is, if you don't Glotan cheese her.

Moveset:
Please refer to the attached image “Balefire Ballerina” for moveset

Exploration note:

The map splits into two Path after the first mob fight, the upward path leads to a heal -> mob fight -> shop -> Elite

The downward path leads to an event -> shop -> Elite

Elite this wave is also The Missing One, not sure why its reused twice this tide. 

Battle note:

To start, Liz  has a permanent passive that makes all your cards have retain.

Liz can also have up to 10 stacks of her passive Emerald ember, and for each stacks she has, she gains bonus damage.

Her “Green Flames” intent changes depending on how many passive stacks she has. 6 passive consumed = 3 hits and 3 burn cards. 3 passive consumed = 2 hits and 2 burn cards. 

Burned cards deal damage to you if you play them, and if they stay in your hand at the end of turn without being played, they are exhausted.

Liz turn 3 intention A.K.A “Dance to destruction” does damage based on the number of cards you have in your hand at the end of turn. Since all your cards have retain because of her passive, she will do like 10+ instances of damage if you have a full hand at the end of turn. But if you discard your whole hand with something like Doll or winkle 3 cost. She will only hit once. So play as many cards as possible this turn.

In phase 2, Liz gain 2 new passives

The first being Emerald Ember generation on HP lost

The second being apply str down effect to you when she receives any str down herself.

Potential strategy:

Glotan: Liz is not as cheesable as pandia,  but you can still cheese her with Glotan exalt damage. The most difficult part is probably getting to the boss——which is really not that difficult if you have a decent team for her. The key for this clear is to save Glotan rouse to charge her second exalt. So you would:
Ready Exalt 1 -> Exalt to kill phase 1 on turn 2  -> Rouse Glotan and ready Exalt 2 -> Exalt to kill phase 2
If you have her image, you can just think about dealing as much damage as possible on turn 3 by abusing her damage scaling and let the pursuit attack kill phase 2. 

Replay(E3 Image with no enlighten on teammates and no saya):

583b2a14-d0ee-38e9-876e-a14184baffb3#E#a

Replay(E3 with saya) : 7ce09bb9-1ff9-3450-a7ef-5f1ca3689ab2#E#a

Saya Mouchette：This is one of the lower investment clears, ultilizing E2 mouchette supported by E0 Glotan and saya. Although Saya is OE in this showcase, you can achieve the same effect without the OE, since she's mainly there for her corrosion.
Replay: 5767e395-823b-33bc-81f0-b3ed38cba5a5#E#a

If you're not using Glotan, then the wave becomes a lot harder, and you would need higher investment to clear it, you could consider borrowing whale mouchette or whale Gmurphy for this wave over W4.

Honorable mention——LV90 Uhvash clear: I don't know who in the right mind would do this, but here it is, the glorious Uhvash 4 turn clear. Ngl, its peak

Replay: 4df96245-6745-3324-9af0-e0a475ac5705#E#a

Just to elaborate a bit since while this infographic is helpful it's not entirely accurate.
There are at least 6 different types of base damage modifiers that are all multiplicative. These are:
**Ability-sourced base dmg**: The two I tested are Kath's "Endless Purgatory" talent (+5% per combust stack) and 24's +20% per Exalt. (for some frustrating reason this multiplies with initial base dmg *before* it's rounded). I don't know if Pollux/Clem/Daff exploration scaling fits here or not, haven't tested.
**Specific Command card base dmg**: Examples include Celestial Beast, Hand of Oblivion. Typically "Base DMG of the wielders Strike/Exalt"
**General card base dmg**: Examples include Data is Flesh, Twisted Knight ballad (passive). Typically "Wielder's cards Base DMG". 
**General base dmg**: Examples include Steppenwolf 6p, Unbearable Freedom, Till the Snow Melts. Typically "Wielder's Base DMG".
Party base dmg:  Examples include relics such as Weeping Pipe, Black Candle, Malignant Child. 
**Dmg amp**: Self-explanatory.
Everything within a specific category is additive but all categories multiply with each other.

There are also *at least* 3 different types of Final damage modifiers that multiply with each other. These are:
**Party final dmg**: Examples include Horla Anger, Vision Corrector Relic. Probably many I'm missing.
**Final dmg**: Examples include Fiamma, Singularity Ultra Beacon. I'm probably missing more.
**Buff sourced final dmg**: "Ablaze" active from Twisted Knight Ballad. 

IDK if category names are intuitive, but they work for me.
In any case, as usual the base dmg modifiers go before dmg add from strength etc, while the final dmg modifiers go after.
This is probably a bit much for an infographic but I figured this info should be here for those seeking to understand how it actually works.
